topics.title: Counting objects to 20
topics.description: Practice one-to-one correspondence by counting collections of up to 20 physical objects, touching and moving each item as it's counted.

topics.title: Reading and writing numbers 0-20
topics.description: Match numerals to quantities and practice writing each numeral 0 through 20 with correct formation and orientation.

topics.title: Comparing numbers with more, less, equal
topics.description: Use counters or two groups of objects to decide which group has more, less, or the same amount and record the comparison.

topics.title: Ordering numbers to 20
topics.description: Arrange a shuffled set of number cards from smallest to largest and largest to smallest, checking for gaps or reversals.

topics.title: Number before, after, and between
topics.description: Use a number line or hundred chart strip to find the number that comes immediately before, after, or between two given numbers.

topics.title: Counting on and counting back to 20
topics.description: Start from any number up to 20 and count forward or backward by ones, using fingers or a number line as a support.

topics.title: Composing and decomposing numbers to 10
topics.description: Break numbers up to 10 into two parts using counters or ten-frames, e.g. 7 as 5 and 2, and record the number bonds.

topics.title: Place value: tens and ones in teen numbers
topics.description: Build teen numbers (11-19) with a ten-frame and loose counters to show they are 'ten and some more', connecting to the number name.

topics.title: Skip counting by 2s to 20
topics.description: Count aloud by 2s while pointing to a number line, noticing the pattern of even numbers landed on.

topics.title: Skip counting by 5s and 10s to 50
topics.description: Use a hundred chart to highlight the numbers reached when counting by 5s and by 10s, spotting the visual pattern.

topics.title: Ordinal numbers first to tenth
topics.description: Line up ten objects or classmates and practice naming and labeling their positions from first to tenth.

topics.title: Addition as combining two groups
topics.description: Physically push two small groups of objects together and count the total to find sums within 10.

topics.title: Addition to 20 using a number line
topics.description: Solve addition problems with sums up to 20 by making hops forward on a number line from the larger addend.

topics.title: Subtraction as taking away
topics.description: Start with a group of objects within 10, remove some, and count what remains to find the difference.

topics.title: Subtraction to 20 using a number line
topics.description: Solve subtraction problems within 20 by making backward hops on a number line from the starting number.

topics.title: Fact families for addition and subtraction
topics.description: Use a set of three related numbers (e.g. 3, 4, 7) to write all four addition and subtraction facts they form.

topics.title: Doubles facts to 10
topics.description: Practice adding a number to itself (1+1 up to 5+5) using matching pairs of objects, building quick recall.

topics.title: Making ten to add
topics.description: Use a ten-frame to bridge through ten when adding, e.g. turning 8+5 into 8+2+3 to make the next ten first.

topics.title: Solving addition and subtraction word problems
topics.description: Read short story problems about combining or separating small groups and choose whether to add or subtract to solve them.

topics.title: Repeating patterns with shapes and colors
topics.description: Identify the repeating unit in an AB, AAB, or ABC pattern made of shapes or colored blocks and say what comes next.

topics.title: Extending and creating patterns
topics.description: Continue a given repeating pattern for several more terms, then invent an original pattern using two or three attributes.

topics.title: Introduction to growing patterns
topics.description: Build a simple growing pattern with blocks (e.g. 1, 2, 3 blocks in a staircase) and predict the next step.

topics.title: Sorting objects by one attribute
topics.description: Sort a mixed collection of objects into groups by a single attribute such as color, size, or shape, and explain the sorting rule.

topics.title: Naming and describing 2D shapes
topics.description: Identify circles, squares, triangles, and rectangles in the classroom and describe them by number of sides and corners.

topics.title: Comparing and combining 2D shapes
topics.description: Compare two shapes to say how they are alike or different, and combine simple shapes to build a new picture or larger shape.

topics.title: Naming 3D shapes
topics.description: Identify and name cubes, spheres, cones, and cylinders among everyday objects, noticing flat and curved surfaces.

topics.title: Positional and spatial language
topics.description: Use words like above, below, next to, and between to describe where objects are placed in relation to each other.

topics.title: Measuring length with non-standard units
topics.description: Measure the length of classroom objects using paperclips or cubes laid end to end and count how many units long each is.

topics.title: Comparing lengths and heights
topics.description: Directly compare two or more objects to order them from shortest to longest or tallest, using words like longer and shorter.

topics.title: Comparing weight using a balance
topics.description: Use a simple balance scale to compare two objects and decide which is heavier or lighter.

topics.title: Exploring capacity: full, empty, more, less
topics.description: Pour water or sand between containers of different sizes to compare which holds more or less and describe full and empty.

topics.title: Telling time to the hour
topics.description: Read an analog clock face and match it to digital times shown on the hour, connecting the short hand's position to the hour.

topics.title: Days of the week and months of the year
topics.description: Recite the days of the week and months of the year in order and place today's date on a classroom calendar.

topics.title: Recognizing coins and their values
topics.description: Identify a penny, nickel, dime, and quarter by sight and state the value each one represents.

topics.title: Collecting and recording data on a pictograph
topics.description: Gather simple survey data from classmates (like favorite fruit) and represent the results using one picture per response on a pictograph.

topics.title: What living things need to survive
topics.description: Sort pictures of plants, animals, and objects into living and non-living, discussing the needs shared by all living things.

topics.title: Basic needs of plants
topics.description: Set up a simple experiment or discussion showing that plants need sunlight, water, soil, and air to grow and stay healthy.

topics.title: Parts of a plant and their jobs
topics.description: Label the roots, stem, leaves, and flower of a plant and describe the job each part does for the whole plant.

topics.title: Plant life cycle from seed to plant
topics.description: Sequence picture cards showing a seed sprouting, growing into a seedling, and becoming a mature flowering plant.

topics.title: Basic needs of animals
topics.description: Discuss and sort what different animals need to survive, comparing food, water, and shelter needs across a few examples.

topics.title: Grouping animals by observable features
topics.description: Sort animal picture cards into groups based on visible traits such as fur, feathers, scales, or number of legs.

topics.title: Animal life cycles
topics.description: Sequence the stages of a familiar animal life cycle, such as a butterfly's egg-caterpillar-chrysalis-butterfly stages, using picture cards.

topics.title: Living vs non-living things
topics.description: Sort a mixed set of classroom and outdoor items into living and non-living categories and justify each choice with evidence.

topics.title: The five senses
topics.description: Identify the five senses and match each one to the body part used, then use each sense to observe a mystery object or smell.

topics.title: Healthy habits and hygiene
topics.description: Discuss daily habits like handwashing, brushing teeth, and sleep that keep the body healthy, and act out the correct steps.

topics.title: Using our senses to make observations
topics.description: Practice describing an object using only sight, touch, smell, or sound, recording observations in simple words or drawings.

topics.title: Introduction to habitats
topics.description: Discuss what a habitat is and match animals to the habitat that best meets their needs, like a fish to water.

topics.title: Comparing forest, ocean, and desert habitats
topics.description: Compare the conditions and animal life found in a forest, ocean, and desert habitat using pictures and short descriptions.

topics.title: Day and night
topics.description: Use a flashlight and globe or simple model to show why we experience day and night as the Earth rotates.

topics.title: The sun's light and heat
topics.description: Discuss how the sun provides both light and warmth, and observe how shadows or warm surfaces show the sun's effects.

topics.title: Observing the sky: sun, moon, and stars
topics.description: Discuss what can be seen in the daytime sky versus the night sky and record observations in a simple sky journal.

topics.title: Describing the weather
topics.description: Observe today's weather and record it using weather vocabulary such as sunny, cloudy, rainy, or windy on a class weather chart.

topics.title: The four seasons
topics.description: Sort pictures of trees, clothing, and activities into the four seasons and discuss how weather changes affect living things.

topics.title: Exploring everyday materials
topics.description: Handle and describe common materials like wood, plastic, metal, and fabric, naming their observable properties.

topics.title: Sorting materials by properties
topics.description: Sort a collection of objects by texture or hardness, such as rough versus smooth or hard versus soft, and explain the sorting rule.

topics.title: Testing which materials float or sink
topics.description: Predict and then test whether different objects float or sink in a tub of water, recording results in a simple chart.

topics.title: Testing magnetic materials
topics.description: Use a magnet to test a set of classroom objects and sort them into magnetic and non-magnetic groups.

topics.title: How materials can change shape
topics.description: Explore bending, squashing, twisting, and stretching different materials to see which ones change shape and which spring back.

topics.title: Push and pull forces
topics.description: Identify examples of pushes and pulls in everyday actions, such as opening a door or kicking a ball, and act them out.

topics.title: How forces change motion
topics.description: Experiment with pushing an object with different amounts of force to see how it affects speed and direction.

topics.title: Simple machines: ramps and wheels
topics.description: Test how a ramp or wheels make it easier to move a heavy object compared to sliding it across a flat surface.

topics.title: Exploring light and shadow
topics.description: Shine a light source on different objects to observe how shadows form and investigate what blocks light and what doesn't.

topics.title: How shadows change
topics.description: Observe how a shadow's size and position change as the light source or object moves closer, farther, or at an angle.

topics.title: How sounds are made
topics.description: Explore vibrating objects like a rubber band or drum to discover that sound is produced by vibrations.

topics.title: Loud, soft, high, and low sounds
topics.description: Compare different sounds in the environment and classify them as loud or soft and high-pitched or low-pitched.

topics.title: Caring for the environment
topics.description: Discuss simple ways to care for the environment, such as recycling and picking up litter, and sort trash into recycling and waste.

topics.title: Making and recording scientific observations
topics.description: Use all five senses to carefully observe an object or event and record findings using drawings and simple labels.

topics.title: Parts of a computer
topics.description: Identify and name the main parts of a computer or tablet, including the screen, keyboard, and mouse, and describe what each does.

topics.title: Turning a device on and off safely
topics.description: Practice the correct steps to power a device on and shut it down safely without damaging files or hardware.

topics.title: Using a mouse: click, double-click, and drag
topics.description: Practice single-clicking to select, double-clicking to open, and dragging to move an icon or object on screen.

topics.title: Using a trackpad and touchscreen
topics.description: Practice basic touchscreen and trackpad gestures such as tapping, scrolling, and dragging to navigate a simple app.

topics.title: Exploring the keyboard
topics.description: Locate letters, numbers, the space bar, and the enter key on the keyboard and practice pressing them one at a time.

topics.title: Logging in safely
topics.description: Practice entering a class login or simple password correctly and understand why passwords should stay private.

topics.title: Opening and closing an application
topics.description: Practice finding an app icon, opening the program, and closing it properly using the correct button or menu.

topics.title: Staying safe online: personal information
topics.description: Discuss what counts as personal information (name, address, school) and why it should never be shared with strangers online.

topics.title: Recognizing safe online situations
topics.description: Look at simple scenario cards and decide whether an online situation seems safe or needs a trusted adult's help.

topics.title: Being kind in digital spaces
topics.description: Discuss what kindness looks like when using shared devices or communicating online, using simple do's and don'ts.

topics.title: What is the internet?
topics.description: Use a simple, age-appropriate explanation and diagram to describe the internet as a way devices connect and share information.

topics.title: Creating pictures in a drawing app
topics.description: Use basic tools in a paint or drawing app, such as pencil, fill, and shapes, to create and color a simple picture.

topics.title: Saving and naming a file
topics.description: Practice saving a completed drawing or document with a clear file name so it can be found again later.

topics.title: Introduction to algorithms
topics.description: Define an algorithm as a set of step-by-step instructions and give everyday examples like a recipe or morning routine.

topics.title: Sequencing everyday tasks
topics.description: Put picture cards of a familiar routine, such as making a sandwich, into the correct step-by-step order.

topics.title: Unplugged coding with directional commands
topics.description: Use arrow cards (forward, backward, turn left, turn right) to direct a partner or toy along a path on the floor.

topics.title: Directing a robot along a path
topics.description: Program a simple floor robot or on-screen character using directional buttons to reach a target on a grid.

topics.title: Introduction to block-based coding
topics.description: Explore a beginner coding app like ScratchJr, dragging and connecting command blocks to see how they run in sequence.

topics.title: Making a sprite move
topics.description: Snap together movement blocks in ScratchJr to make a character walk, jump, or spin across the screen.

topics.title: Debugging simple mistakes
topics.description: Compare a sequence of blocks that doesn't work as planned to the intended outcome, and fix the one block causing the error.

topics.title: Introduction to loops
topics.description: Use a repeat block to make an action happen several times instead of stacking the same block over and over.

topics.title: Spotting patterns in code
topics.description: Look at two short code sequences and identify which blocks repeat, connecting this to patterns learned in math.

topics.title: Typing your name
topics.description: Practice locating and pressing the correct keys in order to type your first name accurately.

topics.title: Introduction to a simple word processor
topics.description: Open a basic word processing app and practice typing a short sentence, using the space bar and delete key correctly.

topics.title: Taking a photo or screenshot
topics.description: Practice using a device's camera or screenshot function to capture an image and find it in the photo gallery.

topics.title: Computers follow instructions exactly
topics.description: Give a partner overly literal step-by-step instructions for a simple task to discover why computers need precise commands.

topics.title: Technology in daily life
topics.description: Identify examples of technology used at home and school, such as phones, tablets, and smart appliances, and discuss their purpose.

topics.title: Spotting computers in the world
topics.description: Go on a picture walk or classroom hunt to find and list devices that contain a computer, from watches to traffic lights.

topics.title: Practicing mouse control through games
topics.description: Play a simple point-and-click game to build accuracy and control when moving and clicking the mouse.

topics.title: Using headphones and volume control
topics.description: Practice putting on headphones correctly and adjusting the volume up and down using on-screen or physical controls.

topics.title: Troubleshooting: asking for help
topics.description: Practice recognizing when something isn't working (frozen screen, no sound) and using polite words to ask an adult for help.

topics.title: Digital drawing with shapes and colors
topics.description: Use shape and fill tools in a drawing app to build a picture out of basic shapes in chosen colors.

topics.title: Naming uppercase and lowercase letters
topics.description: Practice identifying and naming all 26 uppercase and lowercase letters using letter cards, songs, or an alphabet chart.

topics.title: Consonant letter-sound correspondence
topics.description: Practice matching each consonant letter to its most common sound using picture cards and simple sound drills.

topics.title: Short vowel letter-sound correspondence
topics.description: Practice the short sounds of a, e, i, o, and u using picture sorts and hands-on letter tiles.

topics.title: Blending sounds to read CVC words
topics.description: Practice sounding out and blending three-letter consonant-vowel-consonant words like cat, pin, and mud.

topics.title: Segmenting CVC words into sounds
topics.description: Break spoken CVC words into their individual sounds using sound boxes or finger tapping, then match sounds to letters.

topics.title: Reading Grade 1 sight words
topics.description: Practice recognizing and reading common high-frequency words like the, was, and said by sight, without sounding out.

topics.title: Digraphs: sh, ch, th, wh
topics.description: Learn that two letters can make one new sound, and practice reading and sorting words containing sh, ch, th, and wh.

topics.title: Consonant blends
topics.description: Practice reading words that begin or end with two consonant sounds blended together, such as bl, cr, and st.

topics.title: Reading simple decodable sentences
topics.description: Read short sentences built from known sounds and sight words, tracking print left to right with growing fluency.

topics.title: Story elements: characters and setting
topics.description: Identify the characters and setting in a picture book by discussing who the story is about and where it takes place.

topics.title: Retelling a story in sequence
topics.description: Retell a familiar story using beginning, middle, and end, sequencing picture cards or drawings to match the events.

topics.title: Making predictions while reading
topics.description: Look at the cover and pictures of a book to predict what might happen, then check predictions while reading.

topics.title: Answering who, what, where questions
topics.description: Answer simple comprehension questions about a read-aloud text, pointing to evidence in the pictures or words.

topics.title: Identifying rhyming words
topics.description: Listen to pairs of words and decide whether they rhyme, then generate a new rhyming word for a given word.

topics.title: Clapping and counting syllables
topics.description: Clap out the syllables in familiar words and count how many syllable beats each word contains.

topics.title: Onset and rime awareness
topics.description: Break spoken words into their onset (beginning sound) and rime (remaining sounds), such as c-at or fl-ag.

topics.title: Correct letter formation
topics.description: Practice writing each letter with correct starting point, stroke order, and direction using guided handwriting lines.

topics.title: Writing your name and simple words
topics.description: Practice writing your first name and a few simple known words with correct spacing and letter formation.

topics.title: Writing simple sentences with a word bank
topics.description: Use a picture and word bank to construct a simple sentence, choosing words that match the picture's meaning.

topics.title: Capital letters and end punctuation
topics.description: Practice starting sentences with a capital letter and ending them with the correct punctuation mark (. ! ?).

topics.title: Writing a sentence about a picture
topics.description: Look at a picture and write one complete sentence describing what is happening in it.

topics.title: Introduction to nouns
topics.description: Identify nouns as naming words for people, places, and things by sorting picture cards into noun categories.

topics.title: Introduction to verbs
topics.description: Identify verbs as action words by acting out simple verbs like run, jump, and clap, then matching them to pictures.

topics.title: Using descriptive adjectives
topics.description: Add a describing word to a plain sentence (e.g. 'the dog' becomes 'the fluffy dog') to make writing more vivid.

topics.title: Listening and speaking in a group
topics.description: Practice taking turns, listening actively, and sharing a complete thought when discussing a topic in a small group.

topics.title: Nonfiction text features
topics.description: Explore labels, photographs, and captions in a nonfiction book and discuss how they help readers learn information.

topics.title: Fiction vs nonfiction
topics.description: Sort a stack of books into fiction and nonfiction piles and explain the clues used to decide, such as made-up characters versus facts.

topics.title: Forming plural nouns with -s
topics.description: Practice changing singular nouns to plural by adding -s, such as turning one cat into two cats.

topics.title: Following simple written instructions
topics.description: Read a short set of numbered instructions, such as a simple craft or game, and complete each step in order.

topics.title: Introduction to personal narrative writing
topics.description: Write and draw about a real event from your own life, including what happened first, next, and last.

topics.title: Alphabetical order by first letter
topics.description: Practice putting a small group of words or names in order based on the first letter of each word.

topics.title: Reading fluency practice
topics.description: Reread a familiar decodable passage aloud several times to build accuracy, pace, and expression.

topics.title: Place value to 100: tens and ones
topics.description: Represent two-digit numbers using base-ten blocks, showing how many tens and ones make up the total.

topics.title: Reading, writing, and comparing numbers to 100
topics.description: Practice reading and writing numerals to 100 and use greater than, less than, and equal to symbols to compare pairs of numbers.

topics.title: Expanded form of two-digit numbers
topics.description: Break two-digit numbers into tens and ones and write them in expanded form, such as 47 = 40 + 7.

topics.title: Rounding to the nearest ten
topics.description: Use a number line to decide whether a two-digit number is closer to the ten below or above it, and round accordingly.

topics.title: Skip counting by 2s, 5s, and 10s to 100
topics.description: Count fluently by 2s, 5s, and 10s to 100, using a hundred chart to notice the visual patterns each skip count makes.

topics.title: Skip counting by 3s and 4s
topics.description: Practice counting by 3s and 4s using a number line or chart, extending skip counting beyond the most familiar intervals.

topics.title: Odd and even numbers
topics.description: Sort numbers into odd and even groups by pairing up objects, and describe the pattern of digits at the end of each type.

topics.title: Two-digit addition without regrouping
topics.description: Add two two-digit numbers by lining up tens and ones and adding each place separately without carrying.

topics.title: Two-digit addition with regrouping
topics.description: Add two two-digit numbers that require carrying, using base-ten blocks to trade ten ones for one ten.

topics.title: Two-digit subtraction without regrouping
topics.description: Subtract two-digit numbers by working through ones and tens separately when no borrowing is needed.

topics.title: Two-digit subtraction with regrouping
topics.description: Subtract two-digit numbers that require borrowing, using base-ten blocks to trade a ten for ten ones.

topics.title: Mental math strategies
topics.description: Practice quick mental strategies such as adding or subtracting 10, or using friendly numbers, to solve problems without paper.

topics.title: Two-step word problems
topics.description: Solve word problems that require two operations, such as adding then subtracting, and explain the steps taken.

topics.title: Place value to 1000
topics.description: Use base-ten blocks to represent three-digit numbers, identifying the value of the hundreds, tens, and ones digits.

topics.title: Multiplication as repeated addition
topics.description: Model multiplication problems as repeated addition, such as 3 groups of 4 being 4+4+4, using objects or drawings.

topics.title: Building arrays for multiplication
topics.description: Arrange objects into equal rows and columns to build arrays, then write the multiplication fact each array represents.

topics.title: Equal groups and sharing
topics.description: Divide a set of objects into equal groups to solve simple sharing problems, introducing the idea of division informally.

topics.title: Introduction to halves and quarters
topics.description: Fold shapes or divide sets of objects into two or four equal parts to identify and name halves and quarters.

topics.title: Comparing simple fractions
topics.description: Use fraction strips or circles to compare halves, thirds, and quarters, deciding which fraction represents a larger part.

topics.title: Extending and describing number patterns
topics.description: Identify the rule in a growing number pattern, such as adding 3 each time, and extend the sequence.

topics.title: Function machines: input and output
topics.description: Apply a given rule to a set of input numbers to find the outputs, and work backward to discover an unknown rule.

topics.title: Extending growing patterns
topics.description: Build and extend growing patterns using blocks or drawings, describing how the pattern changes from step to step.

topics.title: 2D shape properties
topics.description: Describe and compare 2D shapes by counting their sides, vertices, and identifying right angles.

topics.title: Classifying 2D and 3D shapes
topics.description: Sort a set of shapes by properties such as number of faces, edges, or whether they are flat or solid.

topics.title: Introduction to symmetry
topics.description: Fold paper shapes to find lines of symmetry and identify symmetrical versus non-symmetrical pictures.

topics.title: Measuring length in centimeters and meters
topics.description: Use a ruler or meter stick to measure classroom objects in standard units and record the measurements accurately.

topics.title: Estimating length before measuring
topics.description: Estimate the length of an object in centimeters, then measure it to check how close the estimate was.

topics.title: Measuring mass in grams and kilograms
topics.description: Use a scale to weigh classroom objects in grams and kilograms and compare their masses.

topics.title: Measuring capacity in liters and milliliters
topics.description: Measure the volume of liquid in containers using liters and milliliters and compare quantities across containers.

topics.title: Telling time to the nearest 5 minutes
topics.description: Read an analog clock to the nearest five minutes, connecting the position of the minute hand to the time shown.

topics.title: Introduction to elapsed time
topics.description: Calculate how much time has passed between a start and end time using a clock or number line.

topics.title: Counting money with coins and bills
topics.description: Count mixed sets of coins and small bills to find a total value, and make a given amount using different combinations.

topics.title: Creating bar graphs from collected data
topics.description: Collect data through a simple survey and represent the results by building a bar graph with labeled axes.

topics.title: Reading and interpreting bar graphs
topics.description: Analyze a bar graph or pictograph to answer questions about which category has the most, least, or a specific amount.

topics.title: Introduction to Venn diagrams
topics.description: Sort a set of objects into two overlapping circles based on shared and unique attributes to build a Venn diagram.

topics.title: Comparing animal life cycles
topics.description: Compare the life cycle stages of two different animals, such as a frog and a chicken, noting similarities and differences.

topics.title: Animal adaptations for survival
topics.description: Investigate how specific animal features, such as camouflage or sharp claws, help an animal survive in its habitat.

topics.title: Classifying animals into groups
topics.description: Sort animals into major groups such as mammals, birds, fish, reptiles, and insects based on shared physical traits.

topics.title: Plant adaptations for survival
topics.description: Explore how plant features like thick stems or waxy leaves help different plants survive in their environments.

topics.title: Pollination and seed dispersal
topics.description: Discuss how pollinators like bees help plants reproduce and how seeds travel by wind, water, or animals.

topics.title: Comparing habitats around the world
topics.description: Compare the climate, plants, and animals found in different world habitats such as rainforest, tundra, and grassland.

topics.title: Food chains: producers and consumers
topics.description: Build a simple food chain diagram showing how energy passes from a producer to a consumer to a predator.

topics.title: Introduction to the skeleton and muscles
topics.description: Explore how bones and muscles work together to support the body and allow movement, using a simple model or diagram.

topics.title: Healthy eating and food groups
topics.description: Sort foods into the major food groups and discuss why eating a balance of each group keeps the body healthy.

topics.title: Exercise and the body
topics.description: Discuss how physical activity affects heart rate and breathing, and record observations before and after light exercise.

topics.title: States of matter: solid, liquid, gas
topics.description: Sort familiar substances into solid, liquid, and gas and describe the properties that define each state.

topics.title: Changing states of matter
topics.description: Observe melting, freezing, and evaporation firsthand, such as ice melting or water boiling, to see matter change state.

topics.title: Testing and comparing material properties
topics.description: Test a set of materials for properties like flexibility, absorbency, or waterproofing and record the results in a chart.

topics.title: Reversible and irreversible changes
topics.description: Compare a reversible change, like folding paper, to an irreversible one, like burning it, and sort examples into each category.

topics.title: Simple chemical changes
topics.description: Observe a safe, simple chemical reaction, such as baking soda and vinegar, and describe the signs that a change occurred.

topics.title: The water cycle
topics.description: Trace the stages of evaporation, condensation, and precipitation using a diagram or a simple model in a sealed bag.

topics.title: Landforms and bodies of water
topics.description: Identify and describe common landforms and bodies of water, such as mountains, valleys, rivers, and lakes, using pictures or a model.

topics.title: Exploring rocks and soil
topics.description: Examine samples of rocks and soil to compare texture, color, and composition, and discuss how soil forms over time.

topics.title: The sun, Earth, and moon
topics.description: Use a simple model to show the relative positions and movement of the sun, Earth, and moon in space.

topics.title: Observing moon phases
topics.description: Track the changing appearance of the moon over several nights or weeks and sequence the phases in order.

topics.title: Seasons and Earth's tilt
topics.description: Use a simple model to explain how the tilt of the Earth as it orbits the sun causes the four seasons.

topics.title: Weather tools and measurement
topics.description: Use simple instruments like a thermometer and rain gauge to measure and record daily weather conditions.

topics.title: Climate vs weather
topics.description: Discuss the difference between short-term weather and the long-term climate pattern of a region using examples.

topics.title: Gravity and its effects
topics.description: Test how gravity pulls objects toward the ground by dropping items of different weights and observing the results.

topics.title: Friction and motion
topics.description: Compare how objects move across smooth and rough surfaces to investigate how friction slows things down.

topics.title: Simple machines: levers, pulleys, ramps
topics.description: Test how a lever, pulley, or inclined plane makes it easier to lift or move a heavy object.

topics.title: Magnets: attract and repel
topics.description: Test pairs of magnets to discover when they attract and when they repel, and identify which materials magnets pull toward them.

topics.title: Introduction to simple circuits
topics.description: Build a basic circuit with a battery, wire, and bulb to light it up, and test what happens when the circuit is broken.

topics.title: Sound and vibration
topics.description: Investigate how vibrating objects create sound and how sound travels through air to reach our ears.

topics.title: Light and reflection
topics.description: Explore how light bounces off shiny and matte surfaces and how reflection lets us see ourselves in a mirror.

topics.title: Reduce, reuse, recycle in depth
topics.description: Sort classroom waste into landfill, recycling, and reuse categories and discuss the environmental impact of each choice.

topics.title: The scientific method: question and test
topics.description: Practice asking a testable question, making a prediction, and designing a simple fair test to investigate the answer.

topics.title: Reviewing computer parts and functions
topics.description: Review the function of key computer components, including input devices like a mouse and keyboard and output devices like a screen.

topics.title: Home row typing introduction
topics.description: Practice placing fingers correctly on the home row keys and typing short letter combinations without looking at the keyboard.

topics.title: Typing simple words and sentences
topics.description: Build typing accuracy and speed by typing short words and sentences, checking for correct spelling and spacing.

topics.title: Navigating files and folders
topics.description: Practice opening folders, locating files, and understanding the hierarchy of a simple file system on a shared drive.

topics.title: Saving, renaming, and organizing files
topics.description: Practice saving a document with a descriptive file name and organizing several files into a labeled folder.

topics.title: Formatting text in a word processor
topics.description: Use formatting tools to change text to bold, adjust font size, and change font color in a simple document.

topics.title: Inserting images into a document
topics.description: Practice inserting, resizing, and positioning an image within a word processing document.

topics.title: Creating a simple slideshow
topics.description: Build a short slideshow with a title slide and two or three content slides using text and images.

topics.title: Identifying trusted websites
topics.description: Compare the features of a trusted, kid-safe website to a suspicious one, looking for signs like ads, pop-ups, and unfamiliar addresses.

topics.title: Understanding passwords
topics.description: Discuss what makes a password strong and why passwords should be kept private, even from friends.

topics.title: Being a good digital community member
topics.description: Discuss and role-play examples of respectful online behavior, such as not name-calling or excluding others in a shared game or app.

topics.title: Recognizing information to keep private
topics.description: Practice identifying which pieces of information (full name, address, school, photos) should stay private online.

topics.title: Introduction to search engines
topics.description: Practice typing a focused search query into a kid-safe search engine and evaluating whether results answer the question.

topics.title: Evaluating if online information seems true
topics.description: Compare two simple online sources and discuss basic clues, like matching facts or an unreliable source, that suggest accuracy.

topics.title: Block-based coding in Scratch
topics.description: Explore the Scratch interface, dragging blocks from the palette to the scripting area to build a first simple program.

topics.title: Sequencing commands to move a sprite
topics.description: Snap together movement and turn blocks in order to guide a Scratch sprite along a planned path.

topics.title: Using loops to repeat actions
topics.description: Replace repeated blocks with a repeat loop in Scratch to make a sprite perform an action multiple times efficiently.

topics.title: Using if/then conditionals
topics.description: Add a simple if/then block to a Scratch project so a sprite reacts differently depending on a condition, like touching an edge.

topics.title: Debugging code errors
topics.description: Run a Scratch project that doesn't work as intended, identify which block is out of order or missing, and fix it.

topics.title: Creating an animation or short story
topics.description: Combine sprites, backgrounds, and costume changes in Scratch to build a short animated scene or story.

topics.title: Using events to trigger actions
topics.description: Use event blocks like 'when key pressed' or 'when sprite clicked' to control when different parts of a program run.

topics.title: Input and output devices
topics.description: Sort a list of devices into inputs (keyboard, mouse, microphone) and outputs (screen, speaker, printer) and explain each one's role.

topics.title: Introduction to binary as data storage
topics.description: Use a simple on/off light analogy to introduce the idea that computers store information using just two states.

topics.title: How the internet connects devices
topics.description: Use a simple diagram to show how devices send and receive information across the internet to communicate with each other.

topics.title: Digital drawing with layers and shapes
topics.description: Use layering and shape tools in a drawing app to build a more complex picture with a background and foreground.

topics.title: Creating a digital poster
topics.description: Combine typed text, shapes, and images to design a simple digital poster on a chosen topic.

topics.title: Introduction to spreadsheets
topics.description: Practice entering words and numbers into spreadsheet cells and understand how rows and columns organize data.

topics.title: Understanding email as communication
topics.description: Discuss the parts of an email (to, subject, message) and how people use email to communicate, without sending real messages.

topics.title: Collaborating on a shared document
topics.description: Practice adding to a shared digital document alongside classmates, observing how changes appear for everyone.

topics.title: Programming a simple robot's path
topics.description: Plan and enter a sequence of commands to guide a simple robot from a starting point to a target, adjusting for obstacles.

topics.title: Algorithms as everyday processes
topics.description: Write a step-by-step algorithm for a familiar task, such as brushing teeth, and compare it with a partner's version.

topics.title: Internet safety and screen time review
topics.description: Review key internet safety rules learned so far and discuss why balancing screen time with other activities matters.

topics.title: Mastering letter-sound relationships
topics.description: Review and consolidate all consonant and vowel sounds through quick-paced sound drills and word sorts.

topics.title: Reading multisyllabic words
topics.description: Practice dividing longer words into syllables to decode them piece by piece before blending the whole word.

topics.title: Long vowel patterns with silent e
topics.description: Practice reading and spelling words where a silent e at the end makes the vowel say its name, such as cake and bike.

topics.title: Vowel teams and diphthongs
topics.description: Practice reading words containing vowel teams like ai, ee, oa, and ou, learning the sound each combination makes.

topics.title: R-controlled vowels
topics.description: Practice reading words where a vowel is followed by r, such as ar, er, ir, or, and ur, noticing how the r changes the vowel sound.

topics.title: Reading Grade 2 sight words
topics.description: Practice recognizing and reading a wider set of high-frequency words automatically, without sounding them out.

topics.title: Building reading fluency
topics.description: Reread a passage aloud multiple times to build accuracy, appropriate pace, and expressive phrasing.

topics.title: Identifying main idea and details
topics.description: Read a short passage and identify the main idea in one sentence, then list two or three supporting details.

topics.title: Sequencing events in a story
topics.description: Retell the events of a story in the correct order using transition words like first, next, then, and finally.

topics.title: Comparing and contrasting characters
topics.description: Use a Venn diagram or chart to compare two characters or two versions of a story, noting similarities and differences.

topics.title: Identifying cause and effect
topics.description: Read short passages and identify what happened (the effect) and why it happened (the cause), linking the two with evidence.

topics.title: Making inferences from text
topics.description: Combine clues from the text and prior knowledge to figure out something the author didn't state directly.

topics.title: Understanding author's purpose
topics.description: Read a short text and decide whether the author's main purpose was to inform, entertain, or persuade, citing evidence.

topics.title: Nonfiction text features
topics.description: Use headings, captions, and a glossary in a nonfiction text to locate specific information quickly.

topics.title: Summarizing a short text
topics.description: Write a two-to-three sentence summary of a short passage, including only the most important information in your own words.

topics.title: Complete sentences vs fragments
topics.description: Identify whether a group of words is a complete sentence or a fragment, and revise fragments into complete sentences.

topics.title: Writing a paragraph with a topic sentence
topics.description: Write a short paragraph that opens with a topic sentence and includes two or three supporting detail sentences.

topics.title: Narrative writing with detail
topics.description: Write a short narrative with a clear beginning, middle, and end, adding descriptive details about characters and events.

topics.title: Opinion writing: stating and supporting
topics.description: Write a short opinion piece that states a clear opinion and gives at least one reason to support it.

topics.title: Informational writing about a topic
topics.description: Write a short informational paragraph presenting two or three facts learned about a chosen topic.

topics.title: Editing for capitalization and punctuation
topics.description: Review a piece of writing to find and correct missing capital letters and end punctuation.

topics.title: Using commas in a list
topics.description: Practice inserting commas correctly to separate three or more items in a written list.

topics.title: Plural and possessive nouns
topics.description: Practice forming plural nouns and distinguishing them from possessive nouns, such as cats versus the cat's toy.

topics.title: Past, present, and future tense verbs
topics.description: Practice changing verbs to show whether an action happened in the past, is happening now, or will happen in the future.

topics.title: Using adjectives and adverbs
topics.description: Revise plain sentences by adding adjectives and adverbs to describe nouns and verbs more vividly.

topics.title: Introduction to compound words
topics.description: Identify and build compound words by combining two smaller words, such as sun and flower into sunflower.

topics.title: Prefixes and suffixes
topics.description: Practice adding common prefixes and suffixes, such as un-, re-, -ing, and -ed, to change a word's meaning or tense.

topics.title: Using context clues for word meaning
topics.description: Use surrounding words and sentences in a passage to figure out the meaning of an unfamiliar word.

topics.title: Synonyms and antonyms
topics.description: Sort word pairs into synonyms and antonyms and generate an example of each for a given word.

topics.title: Alphabetizing to the second letter
topics.description: Practice putting a list of words in alphabetical order when the first letters are the same, using the second letter to decide.

topics.title: Speaking and listening in discussion
topics.description: Practice asking a relevant question and giving a complete answer during a structured class or partner discussion.

topics.title: Reading aloud with expression
topics.description: Practice reading a short passage aloud with appropriate pace, volume, and expression for an audience.

topics.title: Multiplication facts up to 10x10
topics.description: Build fluency across the full times tables using flashcards or a timed drill, targeting facts still shaky (usually 6-9s).

topics.title: Division facts related to multiplication tables
topics.description: Practice division facts as the inverse of a known multiplication fact, e.g. 42/6 from knowing 6x7=42.

topics.title: Properties of multiplication (commutative, associative)
topics.description: Show with arrays that 3x4 equals 4x3, and group three factors two different ways to see the product stays the same.

topics.title: Multiplying multiples of 10
topics.description: Multiply numbers like 3x40 by relating it to 3x4 and adding a zero, explaining why that shortcut works.

topics.title: Two-digit by one-digit multiplication
topics.description: Multiply a two-digit number by a one-digit number using an area model before moving to the standard algorithm.

topics.title: Division with remainders
topics.description: Divide a set of objects into equal groups where some are left over, and interpret what the remainder means in context.

topics.title: Relating multiplication and division (fact families)
topics.description: Write the four related facts in a multiplication/division fact family, reinforcing the inverse relationship.

topics.title: Word problems involving multiplication and division
topics.description: Decide whether a story problem calls for multiplication or division by identifying whether groups or a total is unknown.

topics.title: Rounding numbers to nearest 10 and 100
topics.description: Round multi-digit numbers using a number line to see which benchmark ten or hundred a number is closest to.

topics.title: Estimation strategies
topics.description: Estimate sums, differences, and products before calculating exactly, then compare the estimate to the real answer.

topics.title: Fractions on a number line
topics.description: Plot fractions like 3/4 on a number line between 0 and 1, dividing the segment into equal parts first.

topics.title: Equivalent fractions
topics.description: Use fraction strips to find pairs like 1/2 and 2/4 that name the same amount, recording the pattern in the numerators/denominators.

topics.title: Comparing fractions with same denominator
topics.description: Compare fractions that share a denominator by reasoning about which has more equal-sized pieces.

topics.title: Adding and subtracting fractions with like denominators
topics.description: Add and subtract fractions with the same denominator by combining or removing pieces, keeping the denominator unchanged.

topics.title: Mixed numbers introduction
topics.description: Convert between improper fractions and mixed numbers using fraction circles to see the whole-plus-part relationship.

topics.title: Area of rectangles using unit squares
topics.description: Cover a rectangle with unit squares and count them, then connect the count to the length-times-width formula.

topics.title: Perimeter of polygons
topics.description: Measure and sum all sides of irregular polygons, distinguishing perimeter from the area concept covered separately.

topics.title: Distinguishing area vs perimeter
topics.description: Solve paired problems that require finding area in one case and perimeter in another for the same shape.

topics.title: Time: elapsed time word problems
topics.description: Solve multi-step elapsed-time problems (e.g., movie start/end times) using a number line or clock model.

topics.title: Time: converting hours and minutes
topics.description: Convert between hours and minutes (e.g., 90 minutes = 1 hour 30 minutes) using known benchmarks.

topics.title: Money: solving problems with dollars and cents
topics.description: Add and subtract money amounts with dollars and cents, aligning decimal points as an early bridge to decimals.

topics.title: Data: scaled bar graphs
topics.description: Read and build bar graphs where each square represents more than one unit, practicing the scale-reading skill.

topics.title: Data: frequency tables
topics.description: Organize raw survey data into a frequency table, then use it to answer comparison questions.

topics.title: Classifying quadrilaterals
topics.description: Sort quadrilaterals into squares, rectangles, rhombuses, and trapezoids based on side length and angle properties.

topics.title: Classifying triangles by sides and angles
topics.description: Sort triangles as equilateral, isosceles, or scalene, and as acute, right, or obtuse.

topics.title: Symmetry and transformations (flip, slide, turn)
topics.description: Physically flip, slide, and rotate shape cutouts to see how each transformation changes (or preserves) orientation.

topics.title: Two-step word problems with all four operations
topics.description: Solve word problems requiring two different operations in sequence, planning the order of steps before calculating.

topics.title: Patterns in addition and multiplication tables
topics.description: Search a multiplication chart for patterns (e.g., all multiples of 5 end in 0 or 5) and explain why they occur.

topics.title: Introduction to decimals (tenths) via money
topics.description: Connect dimes and pennies to tenths and hundredths of a dollar as a concrete entry point into decimal notation.

topics.title: Problem-solving strategies review and application
topics.description: Apply a toolkit of strategies (draw a picture, make a table, work backward) to a mixed set of challenge problems.

topics.title: Life cycles and metamorphosis (complete vs incomplete)
topics.description: Compare a complete metamorphosis insect (butterfly) to an incomplete one (grasshopper) stage by stage.

topics.title: Structural adaptations for survival
topics.description: Identify a physical structure (beak shape, camouflage color) and explain the survival advantage it provides.

topics.title: Behavioral adaptations for survival
topics.description: Compare a structural adaptation to a behavioral one (migration, playing dead) and classify examples correctly.

topics.title: Ecosystems and interdependence
topics.description: Map out how organisms in a chosen ecosystem depend on each other for food, shelter, or protection.

topics.title: Food webs (building on food chains)
topics.description: Combine several food chains into a food web diagram and trace what happens if one organism is removed.

topics.title: Introduction to biomes
topics.description: Compare two biomes (rainforest and tundra) by climate, plant life, and animal adaptations.

topics.title: Human body: digestive system basics
topics.description: Trace the path food takes through the digestive system using a labeled diagram.

topics.title: Human body: circulatory system basics
topics.description: Explain the heart's role in pumping blood through the body using a simple circulatory diagram.

topics.title: Matter: measuring mass and volume
topics.description: Measure the mass of objects on a scale and the volume of liquids using a graduated cylinder.

topics.title: Physical vs chemical changes (intro)
topics.description: Sort a set of everyday changes (tearing paper, burning wood) into physical or chemical based on whether a new substance forms.

topics.title: Forces and motion: speed and direction
topics.description: Time toy cars traveling a fixed distance to compare speed, and describe motion using direction words.

topics.title: Balanced and unbalanced forces
topics.description: Use a tug-of-war demonstration to show how balanced forces cause no motion and unbalanced forces cause movement.

topics.title: Simple machines: inclined planes and wedges
topics.description: Test how a wedge (doorstop, knife shape) and inclined plane make cutting or lifting tasks easier.

topics.title: Energy forms: heat, light, sound, electrical
topics.description: Sort everyday devices by the primary form of energy they produce or use.

topics.title: Static electricity introduction
topics.description: Rub a balloon on hair to demonstrate static charge, and test what small objects it attracts.

topics.title: Circuits: simple electrical circuit building
topics.description: Build a simple circuit with a battery, wire, and bulb, troubleshooting why it does or doesn't light up.

topics.title: Earth's layers: crust, mantle, core (intro)
topics.description: Build a simple layered model (like a hard-boiled egg) to represent Earth's crust, mantle, and core.

topics.title: Types of rocks: igneous, sedimentary, metamorphic
topics.description: Sort rock samples into the three main types using clues like layering, crystals, or glassy texture.

topics.title: Fossils and what they tell us
topics.description: Examine fossil pictures or replicas to infer what an ancient organism looked like and how it lived.

topics.title: Weather vs climate
topics.description: Compare a single day's weather report to a region's climate description to clarify the difference between the two terms.

topics.title: Introduction to natural disasters and safety
topics.description: Discuss what causes a chosen natural disaster (tornado, flood) and identify basic safety steps.

topics.title: The solar system: order of planets
topics.description: Order planet models or cards by distance from the sun and describe one distinguishing fact about each.

topics.title: Moon phases
topics.description: Use an Oreo-cookie or ball-and-light model to sequence and name the eight phases of the moon.

topics.title: Introduction to gravity and orbits
topics.description: Explain, using a simple model, why gravity keeps planets orbiting the sun instead of flying off in a straight line.

topics.title: Scientific investigation: variables (intro)
topics.description: Identify the variable being tested, kept constant, and measured in a simple class experiment.

topics.title: Data collection with charts and graphs
topics.description: Collect data from a class experiment and represent it in a bar graph, then draw one conclusion from it.

topics.title: Introduction to engineering design process
topics.description: Walk through the ask-imagine-plan-create-improve cycle while building a simple structure out of provided materials.

topics.title: Pollution and conservation
topics.description: Identify a local pollution example and brainstorm one realistic conservation action to reduce its impact.

topics.title: Renewable energy sources (solar, wind, water)
topics.description: Compare solar, wind, and water energy using models or diagrams, discussing an advantage of each.

topics.title: Mini-investigation: designing a fair test
topics.description: Design and run an experiment with one changed variable and everything else controlled, then report results.

topics.title: Loops: nested and repeat-until structures
topics.description: Build a program using a repeat-until loop and compare it to a fixed-count repeat loop.

topics.title: Conditionals: multiple branches (if/elif/else concept in blocks)
topics.description: Build a block program with three or more branching conditions and test each path.

topics.title: Variables: creating and using in block-based projects
topics.description: Create and update multiple variables (lives, score, level) within a single game project.

topics.title: Introduction to functions/custom blocks
topics.description: Create a custom block to bundle a repeated sequence of actions, then reuse it in the project.

topics.title: Event-driven programming (multiple triggers)
topics.description: Build a program that responds to several different event triggers within the same project.

topics.title: Introduction to coordinates and sprite movement (x,y)
topics.description: Move a sprite to specific x,y coordinates and explain how the coordinate system works.

topics.title: Introduction to game design: game loops and rules
topics.description: Design a simple game with a clear win condition and code the game loop that checks it.

topics.title: Designing a simple maze-solving program
topics.description: Program a character to navigate a maze using sequencing, loops, and conditionals together.

topics.title: Introduction to computational thinking: pattern generalization
topics.description: Generalize a pattern from a few examples into a rule that predicts new cases.

topics.title: Debugging complex block programs
topics.description: Debug a multi-block program with more than one bug, isolating and fixing each issue in turn.

topics.title: Introduction to text-based coding concepts (preparing for typed code)
topics.description: Compare block-based code to its typed equivalent side by side to prepare for text-based coding.

topics.title: Introduction to Scratch/Blockly project structure
topics.description: Explore how sprites, scripts, and the stage relate to each other in a Scratch-style project.

topics.title: Introduction to algorithms: searching (finding an item in a list)
topics.description: Search for a target value in a physical or digital list, discussing how many checks it took.

topics.title: Introduction to algorithms: sorting (simple comparisons)
topics.description: Sort a small hand of number cards using simple comparisons, connecting the process to sorting algorithms.

topics.title: Data representation: lists and simple arrays (block-based)
topics.description: Store and access several items in a list variable within a block-based project.

topics.title: Digital citizenship: digital footprint awareness
topics.description: Discuss what a digital footprint is and how online actions can leave a lasting trace.

topics.title: Digital citizenship: evaluating online information (intro)
topics.description: Practice spotting an obviously false claim online and discuss why checking sources matters.

topics.title: Typing fluency practice
topics.description: Practice typing longer passages with attention to accuracy as well as speed.

topics.title: Spreadsheets: basic formulas (sum, average)
topics.description: Use SUM and AVERAGE formulas in a spreadsheet to calculate totals from a small data set.

topics.title: Word processing: formatting documents
topics.description: Format a document with headings, bullet points, and images to improve readability.

topics.title: Presentations: multimedia integration (images, text)
topics.description: Build a presentation combining text, images, and transitions to communicate a short topic.

topics.title: Introduction to internet safety: cyberbullying awareness
topics.description: Discuss what cyberbullying looks like and what steps to take if it happens.

topics.title: Introduction to robotics: sequencing complex movements
topics.description: Program a robot through a multi-step path involving turns, pauses, and speed changes.

topics.title: Introduction to robotics: using sensors for decisions
topics.description: Program a robot to make a decision (stop, turn) based on sensor input.

topics.title: Introduction to hardware: how computers process information
topics.description: Explain, at a simple level, how a computer takes input, processes it, and produces output.

topics.title: Introduction to networks: what connects computers
topics.description: Explain how devices connect to a network using a simple diagram of routers and connections.

topics.title: Collaborative coding projects (team-based)
topics.description: Work in a small team to divide and build parts of a coding project, then combine the pieces.

topics.title: Project planning: pseudocode introduction
topics.description: Write pseudocode outlining a program's logic before implementing it in blocks or code.

topics.title: Creative coding: interactive art project
topics.description: Build an interactive digital art piece that responds to clicks or key presses.

topics.title: Mini-project: build a game with score and levels
topics.description: Build a small game that tracks score and advances through at least two levels.

topics.title: Reading comprehension: identifying theme
topics.description: Identify the theme (life lesson) of a short story and explain what in the story led to that idea.

topics.title: Reading comprehension: summarizing a text
topics.description: Summarize a passage in three to four sentences, including only the most important events.

topics.title: Reading comprehension: inferencing from clues
topics.description: Make an inference about a character's feelings or motive using textual clues rather than direct statements.

topics.title: Understanding point of view (character vs narrator)
topics.description: Distinguish first-person from third-person narration in a text and explain how it affects the story.

topics.title: Comparing and contrasting characters and events
topics.description: Compare and contrast two characters or events from the same text using a Venn diagram.

topics.title: Writing: structured personal narratives with dialogue
topics.description: Write a personal narrative that includes dialogue punctuated correctly to show what characters said.

topics.title: Writing: informative essays with an introduction and conclusion
topics.description: Write a short informative essay with a clear introduction, body paragraphs, and conclusion.

topics.title: Writing: opinion essays with evidence and reasons
topics.description: Write an opinion essay stating a claim and backing it with reasons and specific evidence.

topics.title: Grammar: verb tenses (past, present, future)
topics.description: Identify and correctly use past, present, and future verb tenses in writing.

topics.title: Grammar: pronouns and antecedents
topics.description: Match pronouns to their antecedents correctly and fix sentences with unclear pronoun references.

topics.title: Grammar: compound and complex sentences (intro)
topics.description: Combine two simple sentences into a compound sentence using a coordinating conjunction.

topics.title: Vocabulary: prefixes and suffixes
topics.description: Use common prefixes and suffixes to figure out the meaning of unfamiliar words.

topics.title: Vocabulary: figurative language (similes)
topics.description: Identify similes in a text and explain the comparison being made.

topics.title: Spelling: common irregular words and patterns
topics.description: Practice spelling common irregular words that don't follow standard phonics patterns.

topics.title: Listening: note-taking from an oral presentation
topics.description: Take brief notes while listening to a short oral presentation, capturing the main points only.

topics.title: Speaking: participating in class discussions with evidence
topics.description: Participate in a class discussion, using 'I think... because...' to support opinions with text evidence.

topics.title: Viewing: analyzing images and video for meaning
topics.description: Analyze what a short video clip or image communicates and discuss the choices the creator made.

topics.title: Reading nonfiction: distinguishing fact from opinion
topics.description: Sort statements from a nonfiction text into fact and opinion, explaining the reasoning for each.

topics.title: Reading fiction: understanding plot structure (rising action, climax)
topics.description: Map a story's plot onto a simple mountain diagram identifying rising action, climax, and resolution.

topics.title: Introduction to genre studies (mystery, adventure, fantasy)
topics.description: Identify defining features of a genre (mystery, adventure, fantasy) using examples from a recent read.

topics.title: Poetry: identifying imagery and word choice
topics.description: Identify vivid imagery in a poem and discuss how specific word choices create a picture in the mind.

topics.title: Research skills: using a table of contents and index
topics.description: Use a book's table of contents and index to locate specific information efficiently.

topics.title: Writing process: planning, drafting, revising, editing
topics.description: Move a piece of writing through the full process of planning, drafting, revising, and editing.

topics.title: Presenting: delivering an oral report with visual aids
topics.description: Deliver a short oral report using one visual aid to support the spoken content.

topics.title: Introduction to persuasive language techniques
topics.description: Identify simple persuasive techniques (like using 'everyone agrees') in an advertisement or text.

topics.title: Reading fluency: chapter book reading stamina
topics.description: Build reading stamina by tracking progress through a chapter book over several sessions.

topics.title: Introduction to author's purpose
topics.description: Identify whether a text's purpose is to inform, entertain, or persuade, using clues from the text.

topics.title: Journaling and reflective writing
topics.description: Write a short reflective journal entry about a recent experience or reading response.

topics.title: Introduction to citing sources (simple attribution)
topics.description: Practice a simple form of attribution (this fact came from...) when using information from a source.

topics.title: Peer feedback on writing
topics.description: Give and receive one specific piece of feedback on a partner's draft using a simple feedback frame.

topics.title: Multi-digit addition with regrouping
topics.description: Add numbers with three or more digits using the standard algorithm, carrying across multiple place values.

topics.title: Multi-digit subtraction with regrouping
topics.description: Subtract multi-digit numbers with regrouping across zeros (e.g., 500-238), a common sticking point worth extra practice.

topics.title: Multiplying 2-digit by 2-digit numbers
topics.description: Multiply two two-digit numbers using an area model, then connect it to the standard algorithm's partial products.

topics.title: Dividing multi-digit numbers by 1-digit divisors
